findings.evidence: Mathlib names this shape with the conclusion: `smul_eq_self_of_mem_zpowers` (Mathlib/GroupTheory/OrderOfElement.lean:822), `conj_smul_eq_self_of_mem` (Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Pointwise.lean:507); `grep -rn "theorem smul_of_mem" Mathlib` returns nothing.
findings.fix: Rename to `smul_eq_self_of_mem_smulRange` and `vertexIdempotent_smul_eq_self_of_mem_vertexComponent`; update the three use sites (Module.lean:161, 196; ModuleDecomposition.lean:107, 126, 152, 179).
findings.issue: `smul_of_mem_smulRange` proves `e • x = x` but the name states no conclusion; its sibling `smul_eq_zero_of_mem_smulRange` (line 144) names its conclusion `= 0`, and the `iff` it is derived from spells it `smul_eq_self` (line 110). Same defect at TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/ModuleDecomposition.lean:105, `vertexIdempotent_smul_of_mem_vertexComponent : eᵥ • x = x`.

findings.evidence: Mathlib disambiguates exactly this way in the same area: `mem_corner_iff` vs `mem_corner_iff_mul_left` / `mem_corner_iff_mul_right`, Mathlib/RingTheory/Idempotents.lean:531,535,538.
findings.fix: Rename to `mem_vertexComponent_iff_smul_eq_self` (or `..._iff_vertexIdempotent_smul_eq_self`), matching the general lemma.
findings.issue: `mem_vertexComponent_iff` states the fixed-point characterisation `eᵥ • x = x`, but the general lemma it is proved from calls that `mem_smulRange_iff_smul_eq_self` and reserves the bare `mem_smulRange_iff` for the existential form `∃ y, e • y = x` (Module.lean:89, 110). The same name shape therefore means two different things across the PR.

findings.evidence: Module.lean:189 `theorem smul_coeLinearMap (he : OrthogonalIdempotents e) (z : ⨁ i, smulRange S M (e i)) (j : ι)`; Mathlib keeps every lemma with an `(Complete)OrthogonalIdempotents` hypothesis in that namespace — `OrthogonalIdempotents.mul_sum_of_mem`, `CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents.prod_one_sub` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Idempotents.lean:73, 412).
findings.fix: Rename to `smul_coeLinearMap_smulRange`, and give `sum_smul_eq_self` a subject-identifying name (e.g. `sum_smul_eq_self_of_completeOrthogonalIdempotents`) or move both into a `CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents`/`OrthogonalIdempotents` namespace for dot notation.
findings.issue: `TauCeti.smul_coeLinearMap` is stated only for the family `fun i => smulRange S M (e i)`, but the name mentions neither `smulRange` nor idempotents, so in the top-level `TauCeti` namespace it reads as a general fact about `DirectSum.coeLinearMap`; every sibling in the file identifies the family (`iSupIndep_smulRange`, `iSup_smulRange_eq_top`, `isInternal_smulRange`, `smul_eq_zero_of_mem_smulRange`, `finrank_eq_sum_finrank_smulRange`). `TauCeti.sum_smul_eq_self` (line 166) is the same defect class.

summary: Three naming defects: two lemmas whose names omit the conclusion they prove, one `mem_..._iff` that silently means a different characterisation than its own generalisation, and a top-level lemma name that does not identify its subject.
